newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-POISED PIERCE TO PLAY PAULUS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-POISED PIERCE TO PLAY PAULUS.

text.p: France's Mary Pierce sailed into the semifinals of the Italian Open women's tennis tournament on Friday with only a hint of fatigue after a night of heroics at the Foro Italico.
The Canadian-born 10th seed followed up her floodlit win over top seed Monica Seles on Thursday night with a 6-3 6-4 defeat of Romanian 14th seed Ruxandra Dragomir.
That set up a clash with Austrian Barbara Paulus, returning to Rome for the first time since 1989.
In between, Pierce had started a doubles match with South African Amanda Coetzer that was eventually halted shortly after midnight. It resumed after Friday's win.
"I think maybe my backhand was a bit off today," Pierce explained, discussing a difficult second set in which she led 3-1 before being reeled back in to 3-3.
"I played late last night and I was a little tired."
The fatigue was not evident, with the statuesque Pierce floating elegantly around the court while lashing ferocious forehands past the losing 1997 Hamburg finalist.
"I'm glad I looked that way," the 1995 Australian Open champion replied to an Italian reporter who complimented her on her poise. "It wasn't exactly how I was feeling."
Pierce was also asked whether she tried to look feminine and cool to elicit more support from men in the crowd.
"Yeah," replied the tall 22-year-old with a smile, before a hasty denial. "No, just kidding. I was always brought up to behave and present myself well on court."
Pierce also gave every impression of enjoying her performance, beaming broadly at a particularly well-timed shot in marked contrast to some of the other players in action.
Reigning champion Conchita Martinez had earlier stormed into the semifinals with a no-nonsense 6-0 6-4 defeat of unseeded South African Joannette Kruger.

The Spanish third seed, winner of the Foro Italico clay court tournament for a record four consecutive years, stayed on course for a semifinal clash with second-seeded compatriot Arantxa Sanchez Vicario.
Former world number one Sanchez was due to play unseeded Swiss Patty Schnyder in a late match.
Martinez offered little emotion in her demolition of Kruger. The only real passion on a sun-baked centre court was the occasional scream from Kruger at yet another lost point.
Saturday will see Martinez's fifth successive semifinal at the Italian Open and her sixth in total.
The Spaniard's last defeat at the Foro Italico dates back to the 1991 semifinal when she lost to now-retired Argentine Gabriela Sabatini, who went on to take the title.

Kruger captured just 12 points from Martinez in a lightning first set as the former Wimbledon champion, whose most interesting comments in a subsequent news conference concerned her love of motorbikes, revved up and roared away.
The second set was more of a contest and brought, momentarily, a vague hint of suspense.
Paulus, the 11th seed, made up for her injury-enforced absence by beating Romanian seventh seed Irina Spirlea 6-4 6-2.
Paulus was injured in 1990 and took three years off the circuit as she recovered and had treatment to her knees, ankles and wrists -- seven operations in all.
"I didn't expect too much but it is working," she said. "I think now I'm playing better than in 1990."
